title: Sheik Yerbouti - Wikipedia
notes: Released 3 March 1979, the first release on Zappa Records; mostly live material recorded in 1977 and 1978 with extensive studio overdubs. Personnel: Terry Bozzio, drums, lead (tracks 3, 4, 6, 8, 13, 17) and backing vocals. "Rubber Shirt" combines a Bozzio drum track from one setting with an O'Hearn bass part from another (xenochrony).

title: Bongo Fury - Wikipedia
notes: Zappa, Captain Beefheart and the Mothers, October 1975. Live portions recorded 20 and 21 May 1975 at the Armadillo World Headquarters, Austin; tracks 5, 6 and the introduction to 9 (Muffin Man) in the studio in January 1975. "The first appearance of Terry Bozzio." Personnel: Terry Bozzio, drums; Chester Thompson, drums (5, 6).

title: Walking in L.A. - Wikipedia
notes: Written by Terry Bozzio, produced by Ken Scott at Chateau Recorders, Los Angeles; on Spring Session M (1982), single February 1983, US 70, Top Rock Tracks 12.

title: Muffin Man (song) - Wikipedia
notes: Recorded live by Zappa and the Mothers for Bongo Fury (1975); a studio-recorded spoken opening, then the chorus; closed his concerts for years afterwards.

title: Baby Snakes - Wikipedia
notes: The film of Zappa's Halloween 1977 concerts at the Palladium, New York (released 1979), with Bozzio's drum solo.

title: Transcription: Terry Bozzio / Dancin' Fool - the cool parts (Todd Bishop, Cruise Ship Drummer, 6 February 2017)
notes: The PDF (pdxdrummer.com, read through the Wayback Machine, capture 2025-02-18): the opening instrumental, the same break at 0:54 and the "yowza" interlude after 2:00. Notated for five toms: "he's playing his Rototom set here"; "his right hand on a lower tom and his left on a higher one"; doubles at the start of the yowza section that sound like two bass drums; hats "half-open much of the time", "probably" Paiste 602 (his guess).

title: Terry Bozzio: Melodic Drumming and the Ostinato, Volumes 1, 2 & 3 (Alfred)
notes: Read for section AK (2026-10-15): "self-accompaniment with ostinato patterns ... melodic, harmonic, and even two-part contrapuntal techniques".
